summary_html: Any person (not just mandated reporters) may submit a **voluntary report** to child-protection authorities. CAPTA requires states to maintain mechanisms for intake, confidentiality, and immunity policies tied to federal funding.
authority_html: - **CAPTA (42 U.S.C. §§ 5101–5116)** — requires states to operate intake/report systems that accept voluntary reports and protect good-faith reporters

case_law.method: v1.1.0 case-law rebuild: authorities selected per decision point, each opinion retrieved from CourtListener and read; holding and quote taken from the opinion text; independently re-verified before release. Previous keyword-matched Justia listings were removed.

key_cases.holding: The Court held that KRS 620.030(1) imposes an individual, non-delegable duty to report suspected child abuse directly to law enforcement, the Cabinet, or a prosecutor, so a teacher's and counselor's report to their school principal neither discharged that duty nor entitled them to KRS 620.050 immunity from misdemeanor prosecution.
key_cases.relevance: The Court read KRS 620.030(1) to reach 'any person,' so the same reporting obligation and the same intake channels govern non-mandated third-party reporters.
key_cases.quote: All individuals with firsthand knowledge or reasonable cause to believe that a child is abused have a mandatory duty to report the abuse.

key_cases.holding: The Court held that KRS 620.050(1) grants immunity in either of two independent situations - acting upon reasonable cause in making a report, or acting under KRS 620.030-620.050 in good faith - so a reporter's subjective good-faith belief that she was discharging the reporting duty confers immunity even if that belief was mistaken, and it reinstated summary judgment for the hospital and physician.
key_cases.relevance: The immunity of KRS 620.050(1) extends to 'anyone' who reports, which is what makes voluntary third-party reporting legally safe in Kentucky.
key_cases.quote: a reporter may be "acting under KRS 620.030 to 620.050 in good faith" if the reporter subjectively believed he or she was discharging the duty imposed by KRS 620.030.

reporting_details: Kentucky is a universal mandatory reporting state — any person who knows or has reasonable cause to believe that a child is dependent, neglected, or abused must immediately report to a local law enforcement agency, the Department of Kentucky State Police, the cabinet or its designated representative, the Commonwealth's attorney, or the county attorney (Ky. Rev. Stat. Ann. § 620.030(1)).
